sourceClarifications: 27.7: Both measured forces have only y components, so their full vector equations require B_y=0. The xz-plane field is unique.

27.15: Repeating the trajectory experiment with a proton requires 0.294 T out of the page. The printed odd-answer appendix repeats an electron value with the opposite direction and is inconsistent with the exercise.
27.46: The Hall voltage is 131 microvolt. The sample thickness is 0.23 millimetre. The correct single-carrier density is 3.70e28 per cubic metre.

27.56: The bar and fixed 10-ohm resistor are parallel, in series with 25 ohms. The intended lifting orientation gives bar current 2 A and net acceleration 0.452 metre per square second upward, including its weight.
27.62: The requested estimate states a maximum-torque geometry and an assumed 15-centimetre rotor diameter. A magnetic moment parallel to the field has zero torque.
27.73: Rolling is treated in two stages, corner contact and straight-side contact, with separate potential energies and torque arms.
27.75: The specified field magnitude is 13D/(IA). The field direction satisfying force, torque and negative energy is proportional to (3,4,-12).

27.80: The field is 15 microtesla, not 15 millitesla. At latitude 80 degrees, parallel and perpendicular speeds are 69.5 and 393.9 kilometres per second. The electron turns clockwise as viewed from space toward Earth.
27.81: Values are calculated without premature rounding. The small difference in final position from the rounded appendix is documented privately.
